git-1.mentalModel: A commit identifies a tree snapshot and one or more parent commits. Branch names are movable pointers; they are not separate copies of a project.
git-1.verify: Compare git status with git log --oneline -5. Untracked files will not appear in earlier commits until staged and recorded.
git-1.watch: Git history is not a secret vault. Credentials committed once may remain recoverable even after a later deletion.

git-2.mentalModel: git init creates repository metadata at .git; it does not publish anything remotely. A nested repository can cause confusing ownership of files.
git-2.verify: Run git rev-parse --show-toplevel to identify the actual repository root, then git status --short to inspect the working tree.
git-2.watch: Do not initialize inside an existing checkout accidentally. Locate the parent .git directory before proceeding.

git-3.mentalModel: The index is the proposed next snapshot. git add selects content; git commit records the staged tree and its parent.
git-3.verify: Run git diff before staging and git diff --cached afterward to review precisely what will be committed.
git-3.watch: git add . can include local config or generated files. Use .gitignore and inspect the staged diff before every commit.

git-4.mentalModel: git diff compares working tree to index by default; git diff --cached compares index to HEAD. git log shows ancestry, not file contents alone.
git-4.verify: Use git log --oneline --graph --decorate -10 and git show --stat HEAD to connect a change to its commit.
git-4.watch: A clean working tree does not imply a good build. File integrity, tests, and review remain separate checks.

git-5.mentalModel: A merge preserves both lines of ancestry; rebase replays commits to build a different history. Revert adds a compensating commit.
git-5.verify: For a shared branch, use git revert <commit> and inspect the diff. Practice merge conflicts in a throwaway repository.
git-5.watch: Avoid force-pushing a shared branch to erase errors. Rewritten commit IDs can break other clones, reviews, and signed history.

github-1.mentalModel: Fetch downloads remote refs without changing your checked-out work; pull combines fetch with integration. Push shares reachable local commits.
github-1.verify: Run git remote -v and git branch -vv; verify which remote and upstream branch are configured.
github-1.watch: Never assume origin points to the intended organization. Verify before pushing confidential or unfinished work.

github-2.mentalModel: A pull request compares a head branch with a base branch. Reviewers evaluate both the code change and the test evidence.
github-2.verify: Inspect the Files changed tab and required checks; verify the destination base branch before requesting approval.
github-2.watch: Passing CI cannot prove the design is safe. Check permissions, data flow, rollout, and rollback.

github-3.mentalModel: A fork is a repository copy used for independent development; upstream conventionally names the original project remote.
github-3.verify: Verify git remote -v, fetch upstream, and compare the branches before opening a PR.
github-3.watch: Avoid pushing unrelated local branches or credentials to a public fork.

github-4.mentalModel: Conflicts arise when Git cannot reconcile competing edits automatically. Markers show alternatives, not the final answer.
github-4.verify: After editing the conflicted files, run git diff --check and the project tests, then stage the resolution.
github-4.watch: Removing conflict markers is not sufficient. The combined program still needs semantic review.

github-5.mentalModel: A workflow reacts to events; jobs use isolated runners by default. Tokens and secrets should be scoped to the least privilege needed.
github-5.verify: Inspect the workflow permissions, event triggers and dependency pinning; check the Actions run log for the failing step.
github-5.watch: Pull-request code is untrusted. Avoid exposing elevated secrets or write permissions to unreviewed changes.

docker-1.mentalModel: An image is an immutable filesystem/config template; a container is a runtime instance with a writable layer.
docker-1.verify: Compare docker image ls with docker ps -a and inspect a chosen container's image reference.
docker-1.watch: Deleting a container may discard data held only in its writable layer. Use explicit volumes for persistence.

docker-2.mentalModel: Port publishing maps a host socket to a container socket. The image may declare EXPOSE without actually publishing a host port.
docker-2.verify: Run docker port <container> and docker inspect <container> to confirm the listener and published address.
docker-2.watch: Binding to 0.0.0.0 can expose services beyond localhost. Use 127.0.0.1:hostport:containerport for private practice.

docker-3.mentalModel: Stop requests graceful shutdown before termination; remove deletes the container but not its named volume by default.
docker-3.verify: Review docker ps -a, docker logs --tail 50 <container> and docker inspect before deleting anything.
docker-3.watch: docker exec only works for running containers. Prefer logs and inspect when diagnosing startup failures.

docker-4.mentalModel: Named volumes outlive a container. Bind mounts reference host paths and inherit host filesystem permission considerations.
docker-4.verify: Use docker volume inspect and a disposable data file to confirm persistence after recreating a container.
docker-4.watch: docker compose down -v intentionally deletes managed volumes; do not use it casually on data you need.

docker-5.mentalModel: User-defined bridge networks provide container-name DNS resolution; published host ports are not required for inter-container traffic.
docker-5.verify: Inspect docker network inspect <network> and test service-to-service communication by service name.
docker-5.watch: localhost inside a container means that container, not the host or another service.

engineering-1.mentalModel: A Dockerfile describes image construction. FROM chooses a base, COPY adds files, and CMD defines the default process.
engineering-1.verify: Run docker build -t example:dev . and inspect the resulting image before launching a disposable container.
engineering-1.watch: Use a minimal build context and avoid embedding keys, tokens, or .env files in the image layers.

engineering-2.mentalModel: Docker build cache reuses layers when relevant inputs and instructions are unchanged. Ordering stable steps early saves rebuild time.
engineering-2.verify: Compare build logs after editing source files versus dependency manifests to see which layer invalidates.
engineering-2.watch: A copied secret can survive in an image layer even if deleted in a later instruction.

engineering-3.mentalModel: Compose defines a multi-service application. depends_on controls start order but does not by itself guarantee application readiness.
engineering-3.verify: Use docker compose config to validate the merged model, then docker compose ps to check service state.
engineering-3.watch: Use a healthcheck or application retry logic before assuming the database or upstream service is ready.

engineering-4.mentalModel: Multi-stage builds separate compilers and build tools from runtime artifacts. Digests identify exact image content.
engineering-4.verify: Inspect the runtime image's filesystem and user ID; pin critical base images appropriately.
engineering-4.watch: Small images can still contain exploitable packages. Rebuild, scan, patch, and test regularly.

engineering-5.mentalModel: A liveness probe answers whether a process should be restarted; readiness answers whether it should receive traffic.
engineering-5.verify: Inspect application logs, health status, and resource use separately to distinguish crashes from overload.
engineering-5.watch: A healthcheck that only confirms the process exists can miss broken dependencies or degraded service.

kubernetes-1.mentalModel: The control plane holds desired state and schedules work; kubelet and the container runtime execute workloads on nodes.
kubernetes-1.verify: Use kubectl cluster-info, kubectl get nodes -o wide and kubectl get namespaces for an initial cluster check.
kubernetes-1.watch: A context may point at production. Run kubectl config current-context before writing or deleting resources.

kubernetes-2.mentalModel: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets, which manage Pods. Pods are disposable; stable state belongs outside the Pod filesystem.
kubernetes-2.verify: Use kubectl get deploy,rs,pods and kubectl describe deploy <name> to connect desired and observed state.
kubernetes-2.watch: Editing a live Pod is not a durable deployment change. Update the controller's declarative spec.

kubernetes-3.mentalModel: ClusterIP gives an in-cluster virtual IP; Ingress needs a compatible controller. Service selectors connect clients to Pod endpoints.
kubernetes-3.verify: Check kubectl get svc,endpointslices and verify labels on the intended Pods.
kubernetes-3.watch: A Service with no ready endpoints cannot reach your application even if its DNS name resolves.

kubernetes-4.mentalModel: ConfigMaps are for non-sensitive configuration. Kubernetes Secrets are base64-encoded API objects, not encrypted merely by encoding.
kubernetes-4.verify: Inspect references and RBAC, and enable encryption at rest plus restricted access where appropriate.
kubernetes-4.watch: Do not commit real secret YAML to Git. Prefer external secret delivery and rotation mechanisms.

kubernetes-5.mentalModel: Requests influence scheduling; limits constrain consumption. HPA scales based on configured signals and available metrics.
kubernetes-5.verify: Check kubectl describe pod, kubectl top pods and kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp.
kubernetes-5.watch: CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff and Pending need different investigations. Read Pod events before restarting.

cloud-1.mentalModel: Shared responsibility varies by service model: providers secure the underlying service, customers still configure identity, data, and access.
cloud-1.verify: List who controls OS patching, workload code, IAM and encryption for the specific managed service.
cloud-1.watch: Moving to managed cloud services does not transfer responsibility for excessive permissions or public data.

cloud-2.mentalModel: VMs provide OS-level control; managed containers abstract host maintenance; functions suit event-driven, short-lived tasks.
cloud-2.verify: Compare workload duration, state, networking, scaling, pricing and patch ownership before choosing.
cloud-2.watch: A low idle price does not guarantee a low bill under high request volume, network egress or persistent storage.

cloud-3.mentalModel: Object storage works with keys and objects, block storage with attachable disks, and file storage with shared file semantics.
cloud-3.verify: Confirm persistence, latency, access controls, backup and recovery behavior for each storage choice.
cloud-3.watch: Buckets and shares are not automatically private because application code references them indirectly.

cloud-4.mentalModel: Network routes decide reachability; security groups/firewall policies decide allowed traffic. Public subnets require an actual internet route.
cloud-4.verify: Draw the packet path: source, route table, firewall rules, target listener, and return path.
cloud-4.watch: An open firewall rule is dangerous even if today nothing is listening. Use specific source ranges.

cloud-5.mentalModel: RPO measures acceptable data loss; RTO measures acceptable time to restore service. Multi-zone design improves availability, not necessarily recoverability.
cloud-5.verify: Run a timed restore test with sample data and verify that recovered data meets business expectations.
cloud-5.watch: Backups that have never been restored are unproven. Protect backup access and deletion separately.

platform-1.mentalModel: EC2 provides compute, S3 object storage and IAM access policy. An instance role is safer than long-lived embedded access keys.
platform-1.verify: Inspect trust relationships, policy scopes and resource-level conditions before granting application access.
platform-1.watch: A successful IAM simulator result is not a substitute for testing effective access with the actual principal.

platform-2.mentalModel: Across providers, map the same need to equivalent services while checking differences in policy semantics and networking.
platform-2.verify: Compare VPC/VNet subnets, managed identities, object-store policies and audit logging in an architecture table.
platform-2.watch: Service-name equivalence does not mean permission defaults or security boundaries are identical.

platform-3.mentalModel: Terraform plan previews an intended change; state maps configuration to tracked resources. State is sensitive infrastructure metadata.
platform-3.verify: Run fmt, validate and plan in a non-production workspace; inspect replacements and destroys before apply.
platform-3.watch: Do not store state publicly. Use encrypted remote state, locking where supported, and restrictive access.

platform-4.mentalModel: CI validates changes; CD promotes tested artifacts. Build once, record a digest, and promote that exact artifact between stages.
platform-4.verify: Follow the artifact from commit SHA to build job, registry digest and deployment manifest.
platform-4.watch: Rebuilding from the same tag can produce different bits. Prefer immutable image digests.

platform-5.mentalModel: An SLI is a measured behavior; an SLO sets its target. Error budgets help decide whether to ship or stabilize.
platform-5.verify: Compare service error rate and latency against an agreed window, then inspect correlated deploys and logs.
platform-5.watch: Dashboards without actionable alerts, owners and runbooks rarely shorten incidents.

security-1.mentalModel: Rootless containers reduce risk but do not replace kernel isolation. Drop capabilities and restrict filesystem writes where possible.
security-1.verify: Inspect the image USER, container capabilities, mounts and host-network settings before approving a workload.
security-1.watch: Privileged containers and host mounts expand the blast radius; require explicit justification.

security-2.mentalModel: An SBOM inventories components; vulnerability scans identify known issues; signatures help verify origin and integrity.
security-2.verify: Associate the SBOM, scan report and image digest with the same released build.
security-2.watch: A clean scan is time-bound and incomplete. Update vulnerability data and reassess as new advisories appear.

security-3.mentalModel: OIDC creates short-lived workload identity through a trust policy. Workflow token permissions should default to read-only.
security-3.verify: Check trigger context, audience and subject restrictions before granting cloud federation.
security-3.watch: Never let unreviewed workflow code assume a broad cloud role solely because it runs on your repository.

security-4.mentalModel: Incident response starts with containment, evidence capture and impact assessment, not deleting every unhealthy container.
security-4.verify: Build a timeline from deployment SHA, alerts, logs and change events; rehearse the rollback decision.
security-4.watch: A rollback fixes the symptom only if the old artifact and relevant data migrations remain compatible.

security-5.mentalModel: A secure release connects reviewed source, verified CI, a pinned artifact, least-privilege deployment and tested recovery.
security-5.verify: Trace one release through commit, checks, artifact digest, deployment approval, observability and restoration.
security-5.watch: The best playbook states who can stop a rollout and what signal triggers an immediate rollback.
